import pathlib, tomllib, sys

findings.title: RustSec CI omits the independent WebAssembly lockfile
findings.reproduction: Inspect the linked implementation and its contract. The standing workflow only subscribes to the main and fuzz dependency paths and runs two advisory checks. wasm has its own workspace and a third lockfile.
findings.expected: Changes to all live dependency lockfiles invoke the advisory check, and the scheduled check covers them all.
findings.observed: The standing workflow only subscribes to the main and fuzz dependency paths and runs two advisory checks. wasm has its own workspace and a third lockfile.
findings.impact: The Wasm graph can drift independently without the standing advisory gate. Its current registry packages match versions and checksums in the main lockfile.
findings.recommendedFix: Add the Wasm manifest and lockfile to the triggers and add a third locked advisory check.
findings.requiredVerification: Inspect both event filters and all three check inputs. Run the three lockfile audits on the resulting candidate.

findings.title: WebAssembly self-test gate counts passed checks without checking the total
findings.evidence: Current-source verification at wasm/src/lib.rs:14–20, wasm/run.mjs:13–25, src/self_test.rs:18–19,27–45.
findings.reproduction: Inspect the linked implementation and its contract. The export counts successful checks and discards the total. At the current fixed capacity the recorder silently discards any overflow. If capacity is raised, the runner would also accept 17 passing cases and one failing additional case.
findings.expected: The browser verification checks that all expected known answers ran and that none failed.
findings.observed: The export counts successful checks and discards the total. At the current fixed capacity the recorder silently discards any overflow. If capacity is raised, the runner would also accept 17 passing cases and one failing additional case.
findings.impact: An expanded self-test can hide a failing case behind the current exact-pass count. The current 17-case list still has a directly verifiable outcome.
findings.recommendedFix: Reject self-test recorder overflow, validate the exact number of cases, and require that every case passes.
findings.requiredVerification: Check both a fully passing list and a longer list with one failed known answer.

findings.title: Comparison rustdoc omits the platform and length bounds
findings.evidence: Current-source verification at src/buffer.rs:136–147, src/correct/changes.rs:209–224, src/file/reading.rs:56–71, docs/TECHNICAL.md:54,152.
findings.reproduction: Inspect the linked implementation and its contract. The new rustdoc says clearing follows with protect, although WebAssembly with protect performs no stack write. All three zip folds read the overlapping prefix and separately reject unequal lengths.
findings.expected: Individual equality contracts match the ordinary native fixed-window policy and distinguish equal and unequal lengths.
findings.observed: The new rustdoc says clearing follows with protect, although WebAssembly with protect performs no stack write. All three zip folds read the overlapping prefix and separately reject unequal lengths.
findings.impact: Consumers can rely on an advertised protection or full-input read the comparator does not provide in those configurations.
findings.recommendedFix: Link to the common best-effort native policy and qualify whole-byte scans to equal-length inputs.
findings.requiredVerification: Verify trait rustdoc against the fold, enum-arm selection and exact native/Wasm dependency paths.

findings.title: Cyclic erasure documentation omits plan retention of observed symbols
findings.reproduction: Inspect the linked implementation and its contract. The technical guide says erased values are never read and take part in no result. The owned plan fingerprints the input and records the old symbol for a filled change. Recovered values are independent of the erased symbol.
findings.expected: The docs distinguish whether an erased byte influences recovery from whether plan construction reads or records it.
findings.observed: The technical guide says erased values are never read and take part in no result. The owned plan fingerprints the input and records the old symbol for a filled change. Recovered values are independent of the erased symbol.
findings.impact: A caller can infer an incorrect data-retention boundary from the guide.
findings.recommendedFix: Describe the independence of the solved word and the observed data stored in the plan.
findings.requiredVerification: Compare docs with the marked-shard plan and Changes::values behavior.

The current six targeted Miri runs cover alignment, Buffer equality, lane arithmetic and file bounds on x86-64, i686 and s390x. Strict provenance and Tree Borrows were run separately. OS-backed protected storage is outside the interpreter scope.

The prior 300-second five-target ASan campaign, current x86-64/32-bit predecessor marker evidence and multi-architecture Miri results remain attributed to AUD-009. Claim-specific reuse is based on unchanged source and lockfile bytes only.
The additional feature configurations were run with the normal test profile. The release-profile suite is scoped to the default build.

The separate ordinary 300-second fuzz budget, large arithmetic proof and ignored exhaustive field test were not replayed. The fresh fuzz lane uses the candidate’s 90-second release parameters, with statistics and limitations in the log. No package attestation or package acceptance is asserted.

Native-equivalence and stack cleanup conclusions are scoped to source contracts and the actual logged build and execution rows. The fixed ordinary window does not cover caller frames, registers or application copies.

grants.grant: Protected mappings, page locking and fork/dump flags
grants.admits: OS resource limits can refuse the requested flags. Windows mapping and dump registration affect the process.
grants.narrowestForm: Require exact reported flags for strict calls. Keep ordinary best effort explicit.
grants.order: Allocate and set flags. Strict verifies before writes. Drop wipes writable storage.

grants.grant: Ordinary stack overwrite and joined protected thread
grants.purpose: Reduce residue and run strict work on a protected stack
grants.admits: Fixed window and process/lock resources. Caller views, copies and results have separate lifetimes.
grants.narrowestForm: Use one ordinary scrub per thread scope or one admitted strict stack.
grants.order: Set the thread-local scope. Run, then wipe. Strict joins before mapped-stack cleanup.

grants.grant: SPC re-export, sealed storage and explicit isolation
grants.purpose: Allow checked buffers and downstream isolation choices
grants.admits: Consumers may explicitly change process policy. Processor registers and application state depend on the host.
grants.narrowestForm: Grant typed storage and opt-in process mechanisms.
grants.order: Admit only sealed guarded storage to strict work. Application isolation is a separate step.

grants.grant: Checkout, public Node download and exported Wasm harness
grants.admits: The runner executes pinned tool/action code and a module built from the candidate.
grants.narrowestForm: Read-only repository permissions, no persisted checkout credentials, import-free module and pinned runtime.
grants.order: Build locally, then enter Node and check the exact artifact.

grants.grant: Network tools and release fuzz execution plus artifacts
grants.purpose: Run fixed target campaign before packaging
grants.admits: Build scripts and fuzz targets execute candidate code. Retained fault inputs remain available as normal job artifacts.
grants.narrowestForm: Read-only default permissions and only fuzz artifact outputs on failure.
grants.order: Fetch locked, seed, run every manifest bin, check the lockfile, and allow packaging only after success.

additionalObservations.title: Documented Block pattern compatibility change
additionalObservations.details: Rust constant patterns require structural equality. Manual PartialEq removes patterns based on named Block constants. Ordinary variant patterns are unaffected. The 0.2.0 changelog discloses the deliberate API change.
